question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vector that spans the subspace $H$ as ${h}_{1}.$ 

A vector $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$ belongs to ${H}^{⊥}$ if $x\cdot {h}_{1}=0.$ So, we need to solve the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x\cdot {h}_{1}=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M,$ which is already in row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, we have $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one), so ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ are free variables. From the equation, we get ${x}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}({x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}).$
 So, every vector in ${H}^{⊥}$ has the form 

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}({x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}) \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Therefore, $B=\{[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}$ is a basis of ${H}^{⊥}.$
